paragraphs.text: Split-hand/foot malformation (SHFM) is a limb malformation that affects the central rays of the autopod. It is characterized by absence of the central digital rays, a deep median cleft, and syndactyly of the remaining digits (Gul and Oktenli, 2002; Ugur and Tolun, 2008). Most familial cases are inherited in an autosomal dominant manner (Gul and Oktenli, 2002). SHFM6 is an autosomal recessive form of the malformation (Ugur and Tolun, 2008; Blattner et al., 2010).

checks.evidence_quote: Split-Hand/Foot Malformation (SHFM) is a complex limb malformation affecting the central rays of the autopod.

checks.claim: Split-hand/foot malformation is characterized by absence of the central digital rays, a deep median cleft, and syndactyly of the remaining digits.

paragraphs.text: Zlotogora and Nubani (1989) discussed whether a rare autosomal recessive form of split hand/foot malformation exists. They also proposed an alternative 2-locus model, in which the dominant split hand/foot mutation is controlled by a gene at a second locus. In this model, a dominant mutation at the controlling locus would make the split hand/foot mutation nonpenetrant. Gul and Oktenli (2002) discussed both autosomal recessive inheritance and a 2-locus model for the inbred kindred they studied.

paragraphs.text: Elliott and Evans (2006) noted that SHFM is genetically heterogeneous, with at least 5 loci identified. Using descriptive epidemiology, chi-square analysis, and discriminant function analysis, they identified phenotypic patterns associated with the mapped SHFM loci.
